facts.t: The Income-tax Appellate Tribunal alone carried over 91,000 pending cases
facts.d: Bodies created precisely to be faster than courts have accumulated court-sized backlogs. The Armed Forces Tribunal held nearly 19,000 and central industrial tribunals over 7,000 — figures placed before a Parliamentary Standing Committee.

Articles 323A and 323B were inserted by the 42nd Amendment of 1976, the same amendment that tried to place constitutional amendments beyond judicial review. The tribunalisation of Indian justice began as part of that centralising project.

facts.t: L. Chandra Kumar rescued High Court jurisdiction
facts.d: Article 323A had sought to exclude High Court review of tribunal decisions. The 1997 judgment held such exclusion unconstitutional — tribunals may supplement constitutional courts but never supplant them.

bank.e: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 — the same amendment that produced Articles 368(4) and (5).

bank.q: With reference to L. Chandra Kumar (1997), consider the following statements:
s: Tribunal decisions remain subject to judicial review by High Courts under Articles 226 and 227.
Tribunals may supplement constitutional courts but not supplant them.
The judgment upheld the exclusion of High Court jurisdiction over service matters.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The judgment struck down that exclusion rather than upholding it.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a problem with tribunals?
o: Executive influence over appointments and service conditions
Short tenures with the possibility of reappointment
Excessive constitutional protection of members' independence
bank.e: The complaint runs the other way — tribunal members lack the security of tenure that protects judges.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (holding):
pairs: 1. Recognised the suo motu powers of the National Green Tribunal
2. Tribunal decisions are subject to High Court review
3. Struck down provisions of the Tribunals Reforms Ordinance on service conditions
bank.e: L. Chandra Kumar on review, Madras Bar Association on service conditions, Ankita Sinha on suo motu powers, and Article 323A's origin in 1976.

bank.as: Tribunals were created to deliver faster justice than ordinary courts.
bank.rs: Several now carry backlogs comparable to the courts they were meant to relieve.
bank.e: Both statements are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion — it describes the failure of the purpose the Assertion states. That contrast is the central critique of tribunalisation.

s: Transparent, merit-based appointments to strengthen independence.
Removing High Court oversight to prevent excessive litigation.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Judicial oversight is to be retained with clear guidelines, not removed — L. Chandra Kumar makes removal constitutionally impossible in any case.

bank.q: Which body's 2017 definition describes tribunals as institutions for specialised and faster adjudication?
All of the following are World Bank best practices for tribunal design EXCEPT:
o: Merging all tribunals into the regular court system
bank.e: Consolidation under a single umbrella body is an Indian reform proposal, but merging tribunals back into the courts would defeat the purpose of specialisation.

bank.q: Which tribunal's suo motu powers were recognised in 2021?
bank.e: The National Green Tribunal, in Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai v. Ankita Sinha.

bank.q: With reference to reform of tribunals, consider the following:
s: Consolidation under a single umbrella body is proposed.
Technology integration covering filing, hearings and case management is proposed.
Article 323B allows state legislatures to establish tribunals for specified matters.
bank.e: All three are correct. Article 323B extends the tribunal power beyond service matters to subjects including taxation, land reforms and elections.
